subject: Dedicated reservation banding & GPU staging for Lighthouse Health
messages:

Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@lighthouse.health>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — dedicated reservation sizing and ramp options

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Leadership here asked for a concise set of reservation options we can evaluate alongside our finance team. High level ask: give us 2–3 price/availability bands (small/medium/anchor) with the following for each band:
- cluster size (total GPUs committed)
- minimum guaranteed GPUs (what we pay for even if underutilized)
- suggested ramp schedule (month-by-month activation)
- any warmup credits, burst windows, or soft-fallbacks

Couple constraints to keep in mind: we peak at ~400 concurrent requests/day now, model mix is ~30% chat gen (streaming), 70% embed/semantic search; we prefer a conservative start but need the option to scale quickly by month 3. Also include SLAs and what triggers fallback to hosted variants.

If you can send a short one-pager + a sizing spreadsheet, that'd be ideal. Meeting to review Thursday afternoon works for us.

Cheers,
Spenser
CTO, Lighthouse Health

--

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@lighthouse.health>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — dedicated reservation sizing and ramp options

Hi Spenser — thanks for the clear brief. Attached is a concise options sheet (PDF) plus an editable sizing workbook (XLSX) with assumptions. High-level summary below so you can circulate to finance: 

Option A — Entry band (Conservative)
- Cluster: 8 GPUs (1 x 8-GPU pool)
- Minimum guaranteed: 4 GPUs
- Ramp: Month 0: 4 (warm), Month 1: 8; Month 2+: 8 (steady)
- Use case: low latency dev + controlled production traffic; minimal burst
- Warmup credits: 50k tokens free month 1

Option B — Growth band (Balanced)
- Cluster: 32 GPUs (4 x 8-GPU lanes)
- Minimum guaranteed: 16 GPUs
- Ramp: Month 0: 8, Month 1: 16, Month 2: 32
- Use case: production chat + embeddings at scale; KV cache enabled across lanes
- Burst: 30% burst window during business hours (policy-based)

Option C — Anchor band (Throughput)
- Cluster: 128 GPUs (8 x 16-GPU pools or equivalent)
- Minimum guaranteed: 64 GPUs
- Ramp: Month 0: 16, Month 1: 32, Month 2: 64, Month 3: 128
- Use case: aggressive scaling, high-concurrency inference; dedicated regional lanes + cross-region failover
- Warmup credits & prewarming slots included for first 60 days

Additional notes:
- Fallbacks: we can automatically route to a compatible hosted variant (quantized) if dedicated capacity drops below thresholds; this is configurable as an SLO policy.
- Pricing: workbook has per-GPU-month pricing + per-token delta for hosted fallbacks. We provide stepped discounts on committed months (12/24) — see sheet.
- Attachments: lighthouse_reservation_options_v1.pdf, gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx

Happy to jump on Thu to walk through. I cc'd the sizing workbook owners.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Vivek — this is helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from product/finance: 
1) Our board wants to cap committed GPUs to no more than ~60 GPUs by the end of month 3 unless we hit a revenue trigger. Can you map the Growth band so month 3 stays <=60 (we're open to a staggered increase across regions instead of a single large cluster).
2) For the anchor option what are the SLA credit mechanics if we hit regional outage and need failover?
3) Can you confirm KMS integration for keys and what audit logs are exposed (Marta's on security). I've attached our security questionnaire — can you have your security team fill the relevant bits ahead of Thursday call?

If you can send a revised one-pager that caps month 3 at ~60 for the Growth band, that should keep our procurement folks calm.

Thanks,
Spenser

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reservation banding & GPU staging for Lighthouse Health — internal sizing notes

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Spenser's constraints. Quick internal notes before I reply with a capped growth band: 
- Customer wants month 3 <= 60 GPUs. Suggest we offer Growth (staggered) as: M0: 8 (warm), M1: 18, M2: 36, M3: 60. Spread across 3 regions: 24/18/18 to keep per-region ceilings lower and allow geo-failover.
- Min-guaranteed kept at 50% of committed for month 1/2 to reduce churn risk (so for 60 committed we ask for 30 guaranteed in contract ramp stage).
- Operational impact: KV cache cross-lane consistency is required — Karthik, confirm if current runtime supports cross-pool cache warmup without large cold-start penalties. If not, propose pre-warming slots (billed as warmup credits).
- SLA fallbacks: the hosted-quantized variant can accept spill requests but must be rate-limited; suggest explicit fallback policy in the MOU with credit step-downs.
- Pricing: give them linear step discount: 7% at 12 months, 12% at 24 months; finance will need exact numbers in the workbook.

I'll reply with a revised PDF + updated sizing workbook. Also include the KMS/audit details for Marta — short bullet list is fine.

Vivek

Hi Spenser / Marta — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is v2 of the packet (short one-pager + revised sizing workbook) that caps month 3 at 60 GPUs for the Growth band and includes the KMS/audit summary you requested. Key changes: 
- Growth (capped) path: M0: 8, M1: 18, M2: 36, M3: 60; distribution recommendation: Region A: 24, Region B: 18, Region C: 18.
- Minimum guarantees during ramp: Month 0–1: 50% of committed; Month 2–3: 60% before full activation. Contract language sample included in the doc.
- SLA/failover: cross-region failover available; service credits scale by impact window (10% credit for <1 hr partial degradation, 30% credit for >4 hr regional outage). We include automatic fallback to a verified quantized hosted model with a 5% additional per-token surcharge when used.
- Security/KMS & audit: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / Google KMS / Vault HSM) for model keys and TLS certs. Audit logs: token-level request traces (anonymized), route/instance allocation logs, and admin key-access events retained per retention policy in the console. Marta — we can schedule a short security sync pre-call if you want deeper answers.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, we can draft the mutual action plan and term sheet (I can seed) — link: https://redwood.app/proposals/DL-2027-0843
2) Book Thursday 2:30pm PT for a 45-minute review (I shared a calendar invite).
3) Once MOU agreed, procurement can sign the commitment and we will start regional pool provisioning (estimated 2–4 weeks for M0 ramp).
